hypothesis: Weather foundation models such as Aurora and GraphCast, which autoregressively forecast global atmospheric states at high spatiotemporal resolution, can be fine-tuned at modest computational cost to produce domain-specific outputs (e.g., wind speed, solar irradiance) directly usable as inputs to renewable energy grid scheduling and dispatch optimization pipelines. By coupling the probabilistic trajectory outputs of these models with ML-driven power system optimization, grid operators could reduce the NP-hard complexity of unit commitment and optimal power flow problems, enabling real-time renewable dispatch decisions over multi-day horizons that are currently infeasible with numerical weather prediction alone.
